host_build.upstream_makefile_defect: default FLAGS contain -DPARDISO_5=1, leaving undefined references to pardisoinit/pardiso in the archive; any program linking it fails without a commercial Pardiso 5 library. Build with FLAGS overridden to drop the define.
host_build.peak_rss_bound: ran inside MemoryMax=2G MemorySwapMax=0; no OOM kill observed

determinism: no RNG in Voxelyze 0.9 or in this driver; repeat runs are identical and there are no stochastic replicates

arm_A_verdict.predeclared: at least one pattern >= 0.05 body lengths and not all equal
arm_A_verdict.observed: best travelling at 0.3644 BL, worst uniform at 0.000022 BL; spread spans ~5 orders of magnitude

C_zero_amplitude.note: numerically identical to B, as it must be: both zero the same product cte*amplitude

D_frictionless.note: net_dx and net_dy are exactly 0.0 and COM x,y are constant to 9 decimals across all 241 samples, while COM z ranges 0.009967-0.011017 m. The body is demonstrably active and its horizontal centre of mass does not move. This is the predicted conservation result, not a dead run.

E_zero_gravity.diagnosis: the predeclared argument was wrong, not the threshold. It claimed removing gravity removes the normal force; it does not. With the floor still enabled, actuation itself drives voxels into the floor and generates transient normal force, so Coulomb friction still acts. Arm D, which removes the tangential coefficient, is the control that actually isolates friction, and it gives exactly zero. The threshold was not changed and this arm is recorded as missed.
E_zero_gravity.magnitude: 0.0175 BL, which is 4.8% of the travelling arm and 11.4% of the longitudinal arm

analytic_controls_verdict: 2 positive controls reproduce the closed form at ratio 1.0000 with settle drift <= 6.3e-07; 3 must-fail mutants are rejected at ratios 1.2222, 1.1000 and 10.0000, each while settled and not diverged
settling_sweep_reading: at 20 s simulated the cantilever reproduces Euler-Bernoulli at ratio 1.0000 for n=2,3,4 with drift <= 4.3e-13, and departs to 0.9954 / 0.7983 / 0.2669 at n=6,8,12 with drift rising to 0.081. The departure tracks the drift, so it is incomplete settling of a longer, lower-frequency beam, not a model error. Without the settle gate this would read as a 3.7x stiffness discrepancy.

arm_F_verdict.observed: 0.15318 / 0.15189 / 0.15180 BL at dtScale 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.125; coarsest-to-finest difference 0.00138 BL, which is 0.901% of the coarsest value and 0.909% of the finest; the successive differences fall 0.00129 then 0.00009, consistent with convergence. CORRECTION 2026-11-01: an earlier version of this field wrote '0.90%' without naming the denominator; both figures are now given.

arm_G_verdict.predeclared: no convergence predicted; reported as an open question
arm_G_verdict.observed: 0.15318 BL coarse (5x3x3, s=10mm) versus 0.01878 BL fine (10x6x6, s=5mm), an 8.2x drop

post_hoc_diagnostics.status: NOT preregistered. Run after arm G to explain its gap. Reported as diagnosis, not as confirmatory evidence.

hypothesis_1_global_damping.statement: VX_Material.h:94 gives translational global damping C = zeta*2*sqrt(m*k) with k=E*nomSize, so C ~ L^2 per voxel while voxel count ~ L^-3 and total drag ~ L^-1. Halving the voxel should double total ground drag and suppress motion.
hypothesis_1_global_damping.why_refuted: displacement RISES with zeta at both resolutions, so global damping is not a parasitic drag here; and matching total drag by halving zeta on the fine lattice widens the gap to 15x rather than closing it

hypothesis_2_parity_confound.statement: the longitudinal pattern splits at x < nx/2, so nx=5 gives an asymmetric 2|3 actuator layout and nx=10 a symmetric 5|5 one. Net translation needs a broken mirror symmetry, so the comparison confounded lattice resolution with actuator-layout parity.
hypothesis_2_parity_confound.test: vary nx at FIXED voxel size 10 mm and fixed zeta 0.1
hypothesis_2_parity_confound.reading: odd nx moves 7.6x to 17.8x further than its ADJACENT even neighbours at identical resolution, material, amplitude and duration (nx5/nx4 = 7.65, nx5/nx6 = 17.81, nx7/nx6 = 9.25). Non-adjacent pairs are not part of this claim. Arm G was therefore not a clean resolution test; most of its 8.2x gap is my own encoding. CORRECTION 2026-11-01: an earlier version wrote '7.7x'; 0.15318/0.02003 = 7.6475, which rounds to 7.6.

clean_refinement_test.statement: the travelling-wave pattern sets phase as a gradient 2*pi*x/nx and carries its own asymmetry at any nx, so it has no parity confound.
clean_refinement_test.relative_difference: 2.74% across a 2x lattice refinement and an 8x voxel count
clean_refinement_test.reading: the headline candidate survives mesh refinement; the longitudinal split does not, for a reason that is now identified and measured

extracted_relation.statement: In this configuration, net displacement per actuation cycle is produced by spatial asymmetry of the actuation phase field, not by actuation amplitude alone. A phase field mirror-symmetric about the mid-plane of the travel axis yields roughly an order of magnitude less net displacement than an asymmetric one at matched amplitude, frequency, material and duration.
conditions: Voxelyze 4287e365 lattice, linear elastic E=1e5 Pa, nu=0.35, rho=1e3 kg/m3
Coulomb friction mu_s=1.0, mu_k=0.8 against a rigid floor at z=0
global damping zeta=0.1 to a stationary absolute frame; this is a numerical ground-drag term and NOT a fluid model, so no swimming interpretation is available
5 cycles at 4 Hz, peak linear strain 0.10 from cte 0.01/degC at amplitude 10 degC
bodies of 36 to 360 voxels at 5 mm or 10 mm lattice spacing
validation_data: parity series nx=4,5,6,7 at fixed resolution
two-resolution refinement of the travelling pattern
analytic controls P1, P2 and mutants M1, M2, M3
extracted_relation.NOT_A_BIOLOGICAL_LAW: This is a property of a particular numerical soft-body model under declared parameters. No organism, tissue or cell measurement enters it. It is not evidence about Xenopus, about any computationally designed organism, or about matter.
extracted_relation.known_threat_to_validity: the rectifying ground reaction here is part Coulomb friction and part global damping to an absolute frame; the zeta sweep shows displacement rises with zeta, so the mechanism is not purely frictional crawling and the split between the two has not been measured
